title: What makes data useful?
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: IBM

sections.title: Start with the consumer
sections.body: A pipeline is useful when people can rely on its outputs for a decision. Define the required dataset, its meaning and the time by which it should arrive before choosing tools.

sections.title: Think across stages
sections.body: Source collection, transformation and serving are connected. A clean transformation cannot rescue an incorrectly defined source or an output nobody understands. Record lineage and ownership through the flow.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Choose a daily sales report. Write its freshness target, key fields and the person who resolves a failed delivery.

title: Service boundaries and trade-offs
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: James Lewis & Martin Fowler

sections.title: A boundary is a commitment
sections.body: A service should have a clear purpose and interface. Independence is useful only when a team can build, release and operate the component responsibly.

sections.title: Count the costs
sections.body: Network calls, partial failures, debugging and cross-service data consistency add work. Compare those costs with the value of independent changes and scaling.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Draw two components for a retailer and identify the interface between them. Explain one failure that should not stop the other component.

title: Orchestration as a dependency graph
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: Apache Airflow

sections.title: Describe the dependencies
sections.body: A workflow graph records which tasks must finish before others begin. For example, validate an ingested partition before publishing the transformed table.

sections.title: Task success is not data correctness
sections.body: An orchestrator tracks execution, but your tasks must check the data they publish. Retries also need safe write behavior to avoid duplicated output.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Draw extract, validate, transform and publish as a directed acyclic graph. Add the action to take when validation fails.

title: A useful experiment record
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: MLflow

sections.title: Connect inputs and evidence
sections.body: Record the code and data identifiers, environment, configuration, evaluation metrics and output files for each run. Use consistent naming so comparisons answer a clear question.

sections.title: Separate the record types
sections.body: Parameters describe settings. Metrics hold measurements. Artifacts preserve files such as plots or models. Tracking helps review an experiment; it does not prove the experiment was designed correctly.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Specify two runs that change one parameter while keeping the evaluation split fixed. Name the metric and artifacts you would compare.

title: Keep evaluation data out of training decisions
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: scikit-learn

sections.title: Split before learning transformations
sections.body: Learn scaling or imputation statistics from the training data. Apply those learned operations to held-out data without fitting them again.

sections.title: Check prediction-time availability
sections.body: A field can be accurate and still leak the future. Exclude information recorded after the point where the real system must make a prediction.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: For a churn model, compare last month’s usage with a cancellation date recorded after the prediction. Explain which field leaks the outcome.

title: Build a delivery loop for ML
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: Google Cloud

sections.title: Automate a tested path
sections.body: Connect changes to repeatable checks, training, evaluation and artifact creation. Keep evidence for the candidate that passes the gates.

sections.title: Distinguish the loops
sections.body: Software delivery changes the implementation. Retraining updates a model with data. Both require validation, traceability and an appropriate promotion decision.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Sketch a path from a code commit to a staged model, then draw a separate retraining trigger that reuses the same evaluation gate.

title: Investigate a drift signal
desc: Read an original study brief in the studio, then explore the source for more detail.
creator: Google Cloud

sections.title: Name the reference
sections.body: A distribution comparison only makes sense against a documented baseline and observation window. Track changes in inputs separately from confirmed changes in outcomes.

sections.title: Investigate before retraining
sections.body: A broken data transformation and a changing user population can both shift input statistics. Check quality and context, then use outcome evidence when available.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body: Write a missing-value alert with an owner, first diagnostic step and follow-up metric. Decide what evidence would justify retraining.
